outputs.description: The id of the started Apify run, to feed Apify Results

actorId.title: Actor or Task ID

urls.title: URLs to Scrape
urls.description: The URLs to hand to the run, as a JSON array. Use `return signal.<id>.<handle>` to take them from an upstream node.

waitForCompletion.description: Hold the node until the run finishes, so downstream steps start on finished data. Off hands back the run id immediately and something later has to check.

authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

package.name: apify
package.packageFile:
# FULLY DECLARATIVE. Two nodes, one token.
#
# THE LAST HALF OF THE OLD `crawl` PACKAGE. Its three Hyperbrowser nodes became
# `nodes/hyperbrowser/`; these two are Apify, which shares no endpoint, credential or shape
# with them and was only ever in the same package because both are "web scraping".
#
# I RECORDED THIS PACKAGE AS UNMIGRATABLE ONCE, and that was wrong twice over. The claim was
# that ApifyResults is a stateful iterator, so computation. Reading it properly:
#
#   1. The iterator is DEAD. It emits one item per `continue` signal and declares that input
#      via `getTriggerInputs()`, a hook that exists in NO base class any more — not in
#      plugin-base, not in the engine's CallbackNode. Only two nodes in the tree override
#      it and nothing calls it. So the node fetches the list, emits item[0], and waits for a
#      signal that is never routed.
#
#   2. Iterating is not this node's job. LoopStart/LoopEnd own it, in the marketplace
#      `flow` package, and LOOP_NODES_SPEC.md names the self-continuing CallbackNode as the
#      exact design they replaced. So ApifyResults returns the whole list and a canvas that
#      wants one at a time wires a loop, which is the platform's answer rather than this
#      node's re-invention of it.
#
# The real gaps were two small capabilities, both now built: `offset` pagination, and
# `sha256` in the expression sandbox for the content ids.
#
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/crawl/`.

name: apify
displayName: Apify
description: Run Apify actors and tasks, and read their results
version: 1.0.0
category: ingest
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751511484/gravity/icons/apifyLogo.png

features:
  - Start an actor or a saved task from a list of URLs
  - Read a finished run's dataset, following every page
  - Stable universal and content ids for dedup

allowedHosts:
  - api.apify.com

requires:
  credential: [bearer]
  transport: [json]
  # The dataset endpoint counts ROWS, not pages, so the walk steps by the page size.
  paginate: [offset]
  # ApifyStarter follows the run when asked to wait for it.
  poll: true
  executorVersion: ">=1.1.0"

credentials.apifyCredential.yaml:
# Transcribed from the retired crawl/src/credentials/index.ts, NAME AND FIELD UNCHANGED so
# credentials already stored against `apifyCredential` keep resolving after the move. Note
# the field is `token`, not `apiKey`: Apify calls it a token and the stored rows say token.

name: apifyCredential
displayName: Apify
description: Apify API credentials for starting actor runs and reading their results
documentationUrl: https://docs.apify.com/api/v2

properties:
  - name: token
    displayName: API Token
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Apify API token from console.apify.com
    placeholder: ""

shared.apify.yaml:
# What both nodes share: how to reach Apify, and how a URL list is read.

call: &call
  credential:
    scheme: bearer
    token: "{{ credentials.apifyCredential.token }}"
  headers:
    Accept: application/json
  transport: json
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

# THE URL LIST, normalised. The panel's field is a template that usually carries a JSON
# array as a STRING, and an upstream node may hand over a real array instead.
#
# ONE DELIBERATE DIFFERENCE from the retired parseUrls: a string that opens with `[` and
# fails to parse THROWS rather than being treated as a single URL. The sandbox has no
# try/catch, and the retired node was inconsistent with itself anyway — its own validation
# rejected unparseable JSON with "URLs must be a valid JSON array" while the service it
# called fell back to scraping the broken string. One of those had to go, and the error is
# the honest one.
urls: &urls >-
  return Array.isArray(config.urls)
    ? config.urls.map(u => String(u)).filter(Boolean)
    : typeof config.urls === 'string' && config.urls.trim().startsWith('[')
      ? JSON.parse(config.urls.trim()).map(u => String(u)).filter(Boolean)
      : typeof config.urls === 'string' && config.urls.trim()
        ? [config.urls.trim()]
        : []

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order.
#
# Both read `calls.start`, not `response`. When the wait is switched OFF the second call is
# skipped and the node settles on the first; when it is ON it settles on the second, whose
# body is a different shape. Naming the call keeps one expression true either way, which is
# the whole reason a call has a name.

- emit: runId
  from: response
  value: "return ((calls.start || {}).data || {}).id || ''"

# The LATEST status: whatever the wait ended on, or the start status when nothing waited.
# Reporting the start status after waiting would say RUNNING about a run that had finished.
- emit: status
  from: response
  value: >-
    return calls.finished
      ? ((calls.finished.data || {}).status || '')
      : ((calls.start.data || {}).status || '')
files.api/run.yaml:
# Start the run, and OPTIONALLY wait for it.
#
# Two calls rather than one, because waiting is a choice: the second is gated on the
# toggle, and a skipped call leaves no key, so the events table asks `!!calls.finished`
# rather than checking a sentinel.

# AN ACTOR AND A TASK ARE DIFFERENT ENDPOINTS, told apart by a tilde in the id. That is
# Apify's own convention (a task id is `username~task-name`), and the retired code branched
# on exactly this. It is a URL expression rather than two calls because it is one request
# to one vendor; only the path differs.
- $ref: apify#call
  name: start
  method: POST
  url: >-
    return 'https://api.apify.com/v2/'
      + (String(config.actorId).includes('~') ? 'actor-tasks/' : 'acts/')
      + config.actorId + '/runs'

  # startUrls is the shape every Apify scraper takes: objects, not bare strings.
  #
  # The retired code ALSO spread `actorId` into the actor input on the non-task path, and
  # that is dropped here deliberately rather than transcribed. The actor id says WHICH
  # actor to run, which is the route; it is not something to scrape, so it has no business
  # in the input. The task path never sent it, so the two paths now agree.
  body:
    startUrls: >-
      return (Array.isArray(config.urls)
        ? config.urls.map(u => String(u)).filter(Boolean)
        : typeof config.urls === 'string' && config.urls.trim().startsWith('[')
          ? JSON.parse(config.urls.trim()).map(u => String(u)).filter(Boolean)
          : typeof config.urls === 'string' && config.urls.trim()
            ? [config.urls.trim()]
            : []).map(u => ({ url: u }))

# Only when asked. Apify reports a finished run as SUCCEEDED, and the failure states are
# several, so the terminal test is "stopped being READY or RUNNING" rather than a list of
# ways to fail that a new one could be added to.
- $ref: apify#call
  name: finished
  when: "return config.waitForCompletion === true"
  method: GET
  url: "return 'https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-runs/' + calls.start.data.id"

  poll:
    until: "return ['READY', 'RUNNING'].indexOf(response.data.status) === -1"
    # NO `failed` CLAUSE, deliberately. A run that ends FAILED or ABORTED is not a failure
    # of THIS node: it finished, it said so, and the caller still wants the run id and the
    # status back to decide what to do. Throwing here would discard the id and leave the
    # run unreachable, which is worse than reporting honestly what happened.
    url: "return 'https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-runs/' + calls.start.data.id"
    intervalMs: 5000
    # The panel asks for seconds; the loop counts polls at 5s each.
    maxAttempts: "return Math.max(1, Math.round((config.maxWaitTime || 300) / 5))"
files.config.yaml:
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [actorId, urls]
  properties:
    actorId:
      type: string
      title: Actor or Task ID
      description: >-
        An actor id such as apify/web-scraper, or a saved task id such as
        username~my-scraper-task. A tilde means it is a task, which is a different endpoint.
      default: ""
      placeholder: username~my-scraper-task
    urls:
      # Both, because both arrive: a hand-typed JSON array is a string, and an upstream
      # node's output is a real array.
      type: [array, string]
      title: URLs to Scrape
      description: >-
        The URLs to hand to the run, as a JSON array. Use `return signal.<id>.<handle>` to
        take them from an upstream node.
      default: "[]"
      "ui:field": template
    # THESE TWO USED TO BE A LIE. The retired executor logged "Wait for completion not yet
    # implemented, returning run ID immediately" and returned anyway, so the toggle sat on
    # the panel doing nothing. They are kept rather than deleted because saved workflows
    # already carry them, and they now do what they say: a second call follows the run.
    waitForCompletion:
      type: boolean
      title: Wait for Completion
      description: >-
        Hold the node until the run finishes, so downstream steps start on finished data.
        Off hands back the run id immediately and something later has to check.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    maxWaitTime:
      type: number
      title: Max Wait Time (seconds)
      description: How long to wait before giving up on the run
      default: 300
      minimum: 5
      maximum: 3600
      "ui:dependencies": { waitForCompletion: true }
"ui:order": [actorId, urls, waitForCompletion, maxWaitTime]
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Array of URLs to scrape
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: runId
    type: string
    description: The id of the started Apify run, to feed Apify Results
  - name: status
    type: string
    description: The run's status as Apify reported it at start

credentials:
  - name: apifyCredential
    required: true
    displayName: Apify API
files.node.yaml:
type: ApifyStarter
kind: PromiseNode

name: Apify Starter
category: Web Scraping
color: "#00B4A6"

description: Start an Apify actor or task run over a list of URLs

whenToUse: >-
  Pick to scrape a LARGE LIST of URLs in bulk: the whole list is handed to one Apify run
  rather than fetched a page per request. It hands back a run id and nothing else, so pair
  it with Apify Results to read what the run produced.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NEVER cacheable: this STARTS work and bills for it. Reusing a prior output would hand
  # back an old run id, and the pages it pointed at would silently be the previous run's.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
# STARTS A REAL RUN, which costs Apify credits. waitForCompletion is OFF so the fixture
# returns as soon as the run is queued rather than paying for a full scrape to finish.

testData:
  config:
    actorId: apify/web-scraper
    urls: ["https://example.com"]
    waitForCompletion: false
    maxWaitTime: 300
  inputs:
    signal: ["https://example.com"]
  expect:
    runId: "return typeof output.runId === 'string' && output.runId.length > 0"
    # READY or RUNNING is what a just-started run reports. Asserting a non-empty string
    # would pass on a run that came back FAILED before it began.
    status: "return ['READY', 'RUNNING'].indexOf(output.status) !== -1"
